OBITUARY REFERENCE 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, I refer with profound sorrow to the 
passing away of Shri Arjun Singh, a sitting Member, on the 4th of 
March, 2011, at the age of 81 years.  
Born in November, 1930, at Churhat in Sidhi District of Madhya 
Pradesh,  
Shri Arjun Singh had his education at Allahabad and Agra Universities.  
A lawyer by profession, Shri Arjun Singh had an illustrious 
political career spanning more than five decades. He took keen 
interest in social work and had been closely associated with various 
cultural and social organisations. He started his legislative career 
as a Member of the Madhya Pradesh Legislative Assembly in 1957 and 
served as a Member of that House from 1957 to 1985 and, again, from 
1988 to 1991. He served as Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh on two 
occasions - from 1980 to 1985 and from 1988 to 1989. Under his 
leadership, Madhya Pradesh be came the first State to give lease -hold 
rights upon plots and land to urban slum dwellers. He also served in 
the Government of Madhya Pradesh as Minister of State from 1963 to 
1967, as Minister of Planning and Development in 1967 and as Minister 
of Education from 1972 to 1977. He was Leader of Opposition in the 
Madhya Pradesh Legislative Assembly from 1977 to 1980.  
Shri Arjun Singh served as Governor of Punjab from March to 
November, 1985 and paved the way for ‘ The Rajiv-Sant Longowal Pact ‘ 
known as ‘The Punjab Accord’. He served as Member of the Eighth and 
Tenth Lok Sabha. He was also Leader of the House in the Lok Sabha from 
July, 1991 to November, 1991. Shri Singh served as Union Minister of 
Commerce from November, 1985 to January, 1986; Union Minister of 
Communications from 1986 to 1988 and Union Minister of Human Resource 
Development from 1991 to 1994 and, again, from 2004 to 2009. He also 
served as Chairman of the Department -related Parliamentary Standing 
Committee on Human Resource Development from 2002 to 2004.  
Shri Singh was the Leader of several important delegations to 
international conferences, namely, Indian Delegation to the 26th 
General Conference of UNESCO in 1991, 43rd Session of the 
International Bureau of Education in 1992 and 33rd General Conference 
of UNESCO in 2006. 

 2 
Shri Arjun Singh represented the State of Madhya Pradesh in this 
House from April, 2000 to April, 2006 and, again, from April, 2006 
till his sad demise.  
In the passing away of Shri Arjun Singh, the country has lost an 
eminent administrator and a distinguished parliamentarian.  
We deeply mourn the passing away of Shri Arjun Singh.  
I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence for 
one minute as a mark of respect to the memory of the departed.  
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute.)  
Secretary-General will convey to the members of the bereaved family 
our sense of profound sorrow and deep sympathy.  
MR. CHAIRMAN: As a mark of respect to the memory of Shri Arjun 
Singh,  
a sitting Member, the House stands adjourned till 11.00 a.m. on 
Tuesday, the 8th of March.  
The House then adjourned at five minutes past eleven of the clock till  
eleven of the clock on Tuesday, the 8th March, 2011.
